applicability: Any future session doing structural edits to records or docs
destination: none - declined, reopen as a fresh record on recurrence

evidence.environment: Claude Code remote container, fleet source repository
evidence.source_reference: Group 1 rescan session 2026-08-13: an ad-hoc python slice script reordering corrections in the PROP-002 scan record wrote s[:i]+block instead of s[:i]+block+s[i:], silently discarding ~130 lines; caught by a grep returning empty, recovered from git HEAD

expected_behavior: Structural reorders in prose files use exact-match Edit operations (or are followed by an immediate line-count/diff sanity check against the pre-edit state); ad-hoc slice-and-rewrite scripts are not used on documents whose tail matters
observation: In-place file surgery via ad-hoc string slicing can truncate a document silently and still report success; the Edit tool's exact-match contract refuses precisely this class of error
reason: Verified but over-specialized: a single self-caught slice bug that discarded about 130 lines, recovered from git, with no shipped consequence and no fleet artifact that owns how an agent edits a document. The instruments that bounded it already exist, namely git recovery and the post-edit check that caught it. A new prose rule for one scripting slip would add always-loaded text with no named consumer, which the proportionality gate refuses. Dropped rather than skipped: a second independent occurrence justifies a fresh record, which the evidence gate for returning from an adverse state requires anyway.
